task: Calculate fossil fuel dependency index per US state (50 states + DC) for 2017 and write output.csv

environment.python_modules_available: pandas NOT installed (ModuleNotFoundError) -> use stdlib csv module only
environment.encoding: read source CSVs with encoding='utf-8-sig' (BOM present in headers)

inputs.use: state_name (full name key) + yearly_sunlight_kwh_total (kWh, 2017 vintage file dated 2017-09-08)
clean: drop the single row with state_name == 'NULL' (a non-geographic aggregate row) -> 51 rows left
no blank/missing yearly_sunlight_kwh_total values (min ~1.24e4 kWh, max ~1.98e11 kWh)
inputs.role: roof solar theoretical potential (total sunlight electricity) per state

inputs.transform: sum GENERATION (Megawatthours) over 12 months x 3 fossil sources per state; value already MWh, keep as float
clean: TYPE OF PRODUCER has 6 values; only the aggregate 'Total Electric Power Industry' may be used, otherwise sub-categories (electric utilities / IPP / CHP) double count
do NOT include the 'Total' ENERGY SOURCE row (use it only as a cross-check; fossil sum should be <= Total and Total ~= sum of all sources, diff < 5 MWh)
STATE is a 2-letter abbreviation; map via 51-entry ABB dict; drop 'US-TOTAL'
12 months present for every state in 2017, no missing generation values

inputs.transform: industrial_price_cents_per_kWh_2017 = simple mean of the 12 monthly 'price' values (already cents/kWh)
clean: 2017 industrial has 62 entities: 51 states/DC + 11 aggregates -> exclude ['U.S. Total','New England','Middle Atlantic','East North Central','West North Central','South Atlantic','East South Central','West South Central','Mountain','Pacific Contiguous','Pacific Noncontiguous']
all 51 state entities have exactly 12 monthly values and no blank price
alternative revenue/sales-weighted annual price differs <0.5% for most states (max ~4%, Idaho); simple mean chosen

join.key: full state_name string (already consistent across the roof-solar file and the price file; generation file needs the ABB mapping)
join.expected_coverage: 51/51 entities (50 states + District of Columbia) present in all three sources, zero missing
join.duplicates: none expected; assert one row per state_name before writing

steps: 1. Load solar file with csv.DictReader; drop state_name=='NULL'; build {state_name: yearly_sunlight_kwh_total/1000}.

2. Stream generation file; keep rows YEAR=='2017', TYPE OF PRODUCER=='Total Electric Power Industry', ENERGY SOURCE in {Coal, Natural Gas, Petroleum}; accumulate fossil MWh per STATE abbreviation; convert to full names with ABB.
3. Stream price file; keep year=='2017' and sectorName=='industrial' and stateDescription in state name set; average monthly prices per state.
4. Inner-join the three dicts on full state name; verify set == the 51 expected names (report any extras/missing).
5. Compute fossil_dependency_index = fossil_generation_MWh_2017 / solar_potential_MWh_2017 * industrial_price_cents_per_kWh_2017 (no rounding of inputs; keep float precision).
6. Sort rows alphabetically by state_name; write output.csv with exactly the 5 required columns in the required order and float formatting.

7. Validate: 51 data rows + header; no NaN/inf; all values > 0; spot-check a few states by recomputing the formula independently; compare ranges with data_profile.json quick_stats (fossil gen min ~8,940 MWh DC, max ~339,324,066 MWh TX; solar potential min ~420,338 MWh, max ~198,016,349 MWh; price 4.60-22.94 c/kWh; index 0.171-255.18).

columns.name: state_name
columns.note: full state name, e.g. 'District of Columbia'

columns.name: fossil_generation_MWh_2017
columns.note: coal+natural gas+petroleum, Total Electric Power Industry, 12 months of 2017

known_pitfalls: pandas unavailable -> must use csv module (no df.groupby shortcuts)
forgetting the 'NULL' row in the roof solar file adds a bogus entity
summing all TYPE OF PRODUCER values inflates fossil generation by ~4x
including census-division / U.S. Total rows in the price file inflates the row count to 62
mixing kWh and MWh (solar file is kWh, generation file is already MWh)
matching generation abbreviations to full names requires an explicit 51-entry map
existing_artifacts_note: output.csv and data_profile.json already exist in the workspace as upstream artifacts; the plan's validation step compares the newly computed values against data_profile.json quick_stats for consistency.
